content: I've been working on a few things, ieee754/ryū, sexprs/expansion/hygiene/scheme, hamt, bitmap/bitvec, bignum... I am honestly unsure about what to do with it; I'm like 99% sure this will never go into mathlib for instance, I think it could still be useful for some people though. There doesn't seem to be much of an ecosystem with cs stuff, cslib exists but it's pretty bare?

If it’s all or mostly human written I would encourage you to share your repo and collaborate with others here where it could be contributed to.

If it is AI generated , then you would have more trouble justifying that effort simply because it may be a large amount of effort to unravel the code with you, as opposed to if you wrote it — you’d have an easier time adapting it.

I used heavy automation; idea was a benchmark of the prover system itself which went a bit further than I had originally intended. I think will see less and less people writing stuff like this manually.

This would mostly be useful for a pragmatic use case , do you have some results you’d like to verify , that require these results first ? In that case , if you can check the definitions, you can perhaps get to a stage of verifying your work with AI.

To be integrated into a larger library though, where the goal is organising math knowledge ergonomically , there still needs to be manual work( as of writing this , though I think even in the future there will always be cases requiring a bit of manual work).

right; driven more by pragmatism, I wanted to write stuff in lean and have it be correct, like checker doesnt care if proof is elegant or not i.e. the pretty math can be extracted later. And thanks for the link, wasn't aware of it

Feel free to share your code and such though! People share their code, LLM or not, all the time! I was mostly just sharing my thoughts with regards to it getting into a library.

And just saying it will take a lot more effort to get LLM based code into it , not impossible per se though success rate hasn’t been great historically so far with LLM heavy code.

If you are willing to delve into the sometimes impenetrable looking AI code , you could likely get something out it.
Sure, yeah certainly not targeting mathlib; I guess a better question would have been: is there a place people are just making stuff to use not just to do theory

But your answers are helpful and pretty much resolve this I think. Also side note, I was trying to fight the AI/LLM stuff and not engage with it for so long, and I kept running into it so I just tried to embrace it instead; I think many people probably feel similar—Lean is nice in relation to this because of its absolutism vs non-deterministic inputs. Of course the theorem can just be wrong too but it's a different kind of risk

It is here to stay, opinions vary, but I think it's clear to everyone it can do a lot:
#general > The role of AI companies in large formalisation projects
#Machine Learning for Theorem Proving > Are human mathematicians becoming redundant?
#general > sloplib
#Machine Learning for Theorem Proving > Discussion: How will autoproving impact math?
there are many other discussions out there too if you are curious to see how others may feel about it. It is very topical.
